papers.title_in_file: Verifiable Sampling for Delegated Generative Quantum Machine Learning
papers.what_it_is: A short IEEE QAI 2026 paper proposing a blind and verifiable protocol for delegating quantum generative model inference to a remote quantum server, with a small simulation.

assertions.value: The paper states a verifiable sampling theorem: its protocol samples an output distribution with bounded absolute error and a probability of failure that decreases exponentially with the number of rounds. The proof is a sketch that defers to the authors earlier delegated variational algorithms paper.
assertions.anchor: Section III-A, Theorem III.2 and its sketch proof, p.2
quotes: probability of failure decreasing exponentially with the number of rounds n.
showing that Pr(fail) decreases exponentially with the number of rounds n follows directly from the proof in [18].
assertions.certainty_reason: Only a sketch proof is given here; the full argument sits in the earlier paper [18].
assertions.reader_inference: Because the proof is deferred to prior work, the coordinator may prefer to grade this from the earlier paper rather than this one.

assertions.value: The paper proves a lemma that, for the Maximum Mean Discrepancy loss with a bounded kernel, the absolute difference between the ideal loss and the corrupted loss is bounded in terms of the number of corrupted shots over the total shots and the kernel bound.
assertions.anchor: Section III-A, Lemma III.1 with proof, p.2
quotes: Let L be the Maximum Mean Discrepancy MMDk with a bounded kernel k.
the absolute difference between the ideal loss and the corrupted one is bounded as follows:
assertions.certainty_reason: Lemma III.1 and its proof, p.2.

assertions.value: The authors report simulations of delegated inference for a small Bars and Stripes instance, in which the number of trap detections is correlated with the number of wrong samples.
quotes: We tackle the Bars&Stripes Problem, a common benchmark for quantum generative models
the number of trap detections is correlated to the number of wrong samples
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical simulation result from one setup; Table I numbers are in a table and are not restated.
assertions.reader_inference: The simulation is a toy with a single dephasing attack model, so it illustrates the protocol more than it tests it.

assertions.value: The authors state that the simulation uses a simple dephasing noise model for demonstration, and that end-to-end verifiable training requires every circuit evaluation within a gradient step to share the same graph, which leaves generative models with heterogeneous gradient circuits to future work.
assertions.anchor: Section IV and Section V, p.4-5
quotes: we use this simple model for a demonstrative purpose.
However, the end-to-end verifiable training framework requires that all circuit evaluations within a gradient step share the same MBQC graph
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state this limit of their own framework in the Conclusion, Section V.

papers.title_in_file: Diversity-Aware Ensemble of Quantum-Classical Models via Combinatorial Fusion
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, related work, datasets, circuit search space (Section IV), and the full results and conclusion (Sections VII and VIII). Skimmed, did not read in detail, the classical-model and CFA method sections (V and VI) and the references.
papers.what_it_is: A paper applying Combinatorial Fusion Analysis to a pool of classical models and variational quantum circuits and reporting accuracy gains on four small binary classification datasets.

assertions.value: The authors report that CFA-based hybrid classical-quantum fusion outperformed the best individual model on every one of four binary classification benchmarks, with improvements up to 6.03% in accuracy.
quotes: Experiments on four binary classification benchmarks covering different domains demonstrate that CFA-based hybrid classical-quantum fusion consistently outperform the best individual model on every dataset considered with improvements up to 6.03% in accuracy.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study on four small datasets.
assertions.reader_inference: The best combination was picked from many candidate combinations. In the sections read, the text does not say whether that choice used data separate from the test split; if not, the gains would be optimistic.

assertions.value: On the Pima diabetes dataset the authors report that the best individual model reaches an accuracy of 0.7845 and the best combined model reaches 0.8448.
quotes: The best individual model, AdaBoost, SVM RBF, or StrongEnt, achieves an accuracy of 0.7845
whereas the best combined model reaches 0.8448 under
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one dataset in one study.

assertions.value: On Spambase the authors report accuracy improving from 0.9349 to 0.9407, a gain of 0.58%, and state that the rank-score functions show the models are very similar to one another, which they say helps explain the small improvement.
quotes: performance improves more modestly, from 0.9349 to 0.9407, corresponding to a gain of 0.58%.
models are very similar to one another, which helps explain the relatively small improvement.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one dataset, with the authors own explanation.

assertions.value: The authors state that the quantum circuits are simulated in PennyLane and that evaluating the fusion gains against quantum-induced noise is planned future work.
assertions.anchor: Section IV-A p.4 and Section VIII p.10
quotes: We simulate all circuits on PennyLane
we plan to evaluate the CFA framework against quantum-induced noise to determine if observed diversity patterns and fusion gains remain robust in practical, noisy environments.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state their simulation setup in Section IV-A and the untested noise robustness in Section VIII.

papers.title_in_file: Expressivity of IQP Feature-Map Quantum Kernels via Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, Section II up to the expressivity definition, the statement of Theorem 1, and the conclusions. Did not read the proofs, the discussion of regimes in detail, or the figures and appendices.
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper deriving a Fourier representation of the RKHS generators of IQP feature-map quantum kernels and identifying three bandwidth regimes, checked on synthetic data.

assertions.value: The paper proves that the RKHS generators of IQP quantum kernels are finite sums of trigonometric functions of polynomially transformed input variables, with a finite set of accessible frequencies fixed by the circuit construction and scaled by the bandwidth hyperparameter.
assertions.anchor: Section III (Theorem 1 and Corollary 2), p.3; Section V p.12
quotes: we proved that the generators of the RKHS associated with IQP kernels can be expressed as a composition of periodic trigonometric functions acting on polynomially transformed input variables
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 1 and Corollary 2 in Section III; restated in the Conclusions.
assertions.reader_inference: I read the statement of Theorem 1 and the authors summary, not the proofs.

assertions.value: The authors report three bandwidth regimes: at small bandwidth the generators are localised and the kernel behaves comparably to a Gaussian kernel, at intermediate values they are multimodal, and at large values their periodic character dominates.
quotes: At small bandwidth the generators are localised and the kernel behaves comparably to a Gaussian kernel;
at intermediate values they become multimodal, assigning high similarity to points that are distant in input space;
at large values their periodic character dominates
assertions.certainty_reason: The regimes are a qualitative characterisation supported by synthetic-data experiments.
assertions.reader_inference: The authors tie the practical benefit to matching the data structure, so a gain over a Gaussian kernel is not expected on generic data.

assertions.value: The authors state that, in their numerical experiments, the expressive power of IQP kernels translates into a practical benefit only when the accessible frequencies match the structure of the data.
quotes: expressive power translates into a practical benefit only when the accessible frequencies match with the structure of the data
assertions.certainty_reason: An author conclusion drawn from synthetic experiments.

assertions.value: The authors state that the numerical experiments are restricted to synthetic datasets with controlled periodic or multimodal structure, and that the theoretical characterisation applies specifically to IQP feature maps.
quotes: we acknowledge that the numerical experiments are restricted to synthetic datasets with controlled periodic or multimodal structure
the theoretical characterisation applies specifically to IQP feature maps
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state both limits in the Conclusions, Section V.

papers.title_in_file: Supervised Learning with Quantum Hamiltonian Embeddings
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, the statement of Theorem 2 and Corollary 3, Section IV (experiments) and Section V (discussion). Did not read the appendices (proofs, hardness construction, surrogate separations) or Sections II and III in full.
papers.what_it_is: An IBM-led paper introducing a supervised quantum learning framework that encodes a training set into one parameterized Hamiltonian, with generalization bounds, a conditional hardness construction, and Fashion-MNIST experiments including IBM Heron hardware.

assertions.value: The paper proves a generalization bound, conditional on training reaching a sufficiently low-energy approximate ground state: for fixed generalization error, the required dataset size scales linearly, up to logarithmic factors, with the number of qubits and variational parameters.
assertions.anchor: Section III-A, Theorem 2 and Corollary 3, pp.12-14; Introduction p.3
quotes: If training yields a sufficiently low-energy approximate ground state, matrix Hoeffding inequalities and covering number arguments establish generalization to unseen inputs.
We show that for fixed generalization error, the required dataset size scales linearly, up to logarithmic factors, with the number of qubits and variational parameters.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 2 and Corollary 3, Section III A.
assertions.reader_inference: The authors disclose that language models assisted parts of the analytical work, including selected proof steps, which they say they verified.

assertions.value: The authors state that, under standard cryptographic assumptions, structured instances yield explicit learning problems that a quantum processor can solve within the Hamiltonian embedding framework while they remain classically hard.
assertions.anchor: Introduction p.3; Section III-C and Appendix E (not read)
quotes: Under standard cryptographic assumptions, these instances yield explicit learning problems solvable on a quantum processor within the Hamiltonian embedding framework, while remaining classically hard.
assertions.certainty_reason: I read the statement in the Introduction but not the proof in Appendix E, so I do not suggest a higher grade.
assertions.reader_inference: The hardness holds for constructed cryptographic problems; the authors say it is unclear whether the framework helps on generic tasks.

assertions.value: On binary Fashion-MNIST (dress versus shirt), the authors report that the classical iterative solver proxy for their framework achieves a higher mean test accuracy than the best reported quantum kernel baseline, by margins from 0.018 to 0.067, while the best classical baseline, a support vector classifier with a radial basis function kernel, reaches about 0.946.
quotes: achieves a higher mean test accuracy than the best reported quantum kernel baseline, with margins ranging from 0.018 to 0.067.
with a radial basis function kernel, performs the best, reaching an accuracy of approximately 0.946
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one benchmark; the proxy is a classical solver, not hardware.
assertions.reader_inference: The best classical model beats the framework, so the experiments show competitiveness with quantum kernels, not an advantage over classical methods.

assertions.value: The authors state that for generic learning tasks it remains unclear when the inductive bias of Hamiltonian embedding offers an advantage over alternative classical or quantum methods.
quotes: For generic learning tasks, however, it remains unclear when the inductive bias of Hamiltonian embedding offers an advantage over alternative classical or quantum methods.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state this open question in the Discussion, Section V.
